scenario.prompt_to_agent:
A user on the CS LAB 1 PC (192.168.2.3) reports they cannot reach
the Server Room (1.0.0.x) or the Internet Lab (128.168.0.x). The
IT Department PCs are also affected. Other zones (Office, Principle,
Internet Lab itself) can still reach each other. What's wrong?
scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router0 ripd daemon
Mechanism: router0 is the only L3 hop between IT Dept
  (192.168.1.0/24), CS Dept (192.168.2.0/24), and the rest
  of the network (reached via Serial2/0 to router1). When
  ripd dies on router0, router1 ages out the 192.168.1.0/24
  and 192.168.2.0/24 prefixes, and router0 itself stops
  learning the 1.0.0.0/8 / 128.168.0.0/16 / 192.168.3.0/24
  / 192.168.4.0/24 prefixes from router1. IT + CS PCs become
  isolated from everything beyond router0.
Localization: router0
Root cause: RIP routing daemon (ripd) not running on router0
Fix: restart FRR AND re-apply the `router rip` configuration on router0 (see [FIX] -- a bare restart alone does not restore the vtysh-applied config).

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): ripd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router rip` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ripd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the rip configuration is missing/empty on router0" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart FRR / the ripd daemon on router0 (e.g. `/etc/init.d/frr restart` on
router0). Once ripd is running again it re-learns the remote prefixes and
re-advertises 192.168.1.0/24 and 192.168.2.0/24, restoring IT Dept and CS Dept
reachability.

NOTE (lab-verified 2026-07-03): this lab applies FRR config via vtysh at boot (there is no /etc/frr/frr.conf), so `/etc/init.d/frr restart` alone brings ripd back CONFIG-LESS and the rip service stays broken. The complete remediation is to (re)start FRR/ripd AND re-apply the `router rip` configuration (network statements) on router0. A proposal that restores the missing rip configuration is a correct fix; a bare daemon restart without restoring the config is incomplete.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The RIP daemon (ripd) is completely absent from router0. The device's
/etc/frr/daemons file has ripd=no, no /etc/frr/frr.conf exists, and
ps confirms only zebra/mgmtd/staticd are running — ripd was never
started. As a result, router0's FIB contains only its three
directly-connected prefixes (192.168.1.0/24 for the IT LAN,
192.168.2.0/24 for the CS LAN, and 10.0.0.0/8 for the WAN to
router1). It has no learned routes to the Server Room (1.0.0.0/8,
attached to router2) or the Internet Lab (128.168.0.0/16, also on
router2), nor to the Office or Principle subnets on router1.

When a CS or IT host sends traffic to those destinations, the packet
reaches router0 (the first-hop gateway at 192.168.2.1 / 192.168.1.1),
which finds no matching FIB entry and immediately returns an ICMP
"Destination Net Unreachable" — confirmed by live pings from both
cs_lab1 and it_lab1. Office and Principle hosts are unaffected because
they sit behind router1, which has a complete RIP table (learned from
router1 ↔ router2 peering) and can forward among all zones without
ever transiting router0.

Root cause: ripd is disabled on router0, leaving it with no dynamic
routing protocol and no knowledge of any non-directly-connected prefix.

Fix: Set ripd=yes in /etc/frr/daemons on router0, create
/etc/frr/frr.conf with a "router rip" block advertising networks
192.168.1.0/24, 192.168.2.0/24, and 10.0.0.0/8, then restart FRR
(service frr restart). Router0 will then exchange RIP updates with
router1 over the 10.0.0.0/8 WAN and populate its full routing table.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies router0 as the affected device throughout the diagnosis.
Agent explicitly identifies the RIP daemon (ripd) / RIP routing as the affected component and root cause (ripd disabled/not running).
The report explicitly notes IT and CS hosts are isolated (confirmed by pings) while Office/Principle hosts behind router1 remain unaffected.
Enabling ripd, creating/applying the 'router rip' network statements, and restarting FRR will restore RIP and re-learn/advertise the missing routes as required.

The agent's claims are directly supported by command outputs in the log (ps, cat /etc/frr/..., vtysh show running-config, ping failures/successes) and its inferences (ripd absent → no RIP routes → isolation of IT/CS) follow logically; essential alternative causes were checked.
